Good work deserves to be seen. 💚

That’s why AbilityMade began: two students wanted to help more people discover the work of disabled artisans. Today, our website brings together handmade gifts, craft objects, and artwork while supporting people with intellectual, developmental, and physical disabilities.

Come have a look around at abilitymade.net. You might find something that feels very you.

Are you a bright-color person, or do you always reach for neutrals? 🌈

We have a soft spot for the little details. AbilityMade’s beaded collection includes sculptures and bracelets, with pieces ranging from a green tree to a flower-filled basket.

Take a closer look at the actual creations at abilitymade.net, and tell us which one catches your eye.

Photo: Magda Ehlers / Pexels. Bead inspiration, not an AbilityMade product photo.

#AbilityMade #Beadwork #HandmadeDetails

posts.caption:
A small detail can be the thing you love most.

A pattern. A color pairing. The way a piece feels in your hand. AbilityMade’s story is rooted in artisans spending time learning techniques and carefully making their work by hand. That care is part of what we hope you notice.

Read the full story at abilitymade.net/our-story-in-full.html. What makes a handmade piece special to you?

posts.caption:
You know that feeling when you find a gift and immediately think of someone? 🎁

That’s the kind of browsing we love. Explore frame clutch purses, diamond paintings, beaded pieces, and artwork at AbilityMade. There’s room for both the practical-gift person and the color-on-every-wall person.

Start at abilitymade.net. If something catches your eye, use the site’s purchase-request option to get in touch.

“How can I help?” There’s more than one way. 💌

Share AbilityMade with a friend who loves handmade things. Browse the artists’ work. Sign up for occasional news and promotions through the newsletter on our website.

And if you have an idea for supporting the mission, we’d love to hear it: AbilityMade@gmail.com.

A simple introduction can help someone new discover an artist’s work. Who would you share this with?
